question: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

options.opd: Deposition of crystals in the joint

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Right knee pain" -> "swelling and erythema" -> "fluctuance over inferior patella" -> "possible joint effusion" -> "suggests inflammation or infection" -> "absence of joint line tenderness" -> "less likely to be meniscal injury" -> "possible infection of the joint" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Right knee pain" -> "swelling and erythema" -> "fluctuance over inferior patella" -> "indicates fluid accumulation" -> "could be due to inflammation or infection" -> "tenderness on patella" -> "possible inflammation of periarticular structures" -> "less likely to be crystal deposition" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Right knee pain" -> "swelling and erythema" -> "fluctuance over inferior patella" -> "suggests joint effusion" -> "could be due to infection or inflammation" -> "absence of trauma other than minor toe injury" -> "less likely to be due to trauma" -> "more consistent with infection of the joint" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Right knee pain" -> "swelling and erythema" -> "fluctuance over inferior patella" -> "indicates possible bursitis" -> "inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac" -> "could explain swelling and tenderness" -> "less likely to be crystal deposition or infection" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's symptoms of knee pain, swelling, erythema, and fluctuance over the inferior patella suggest an inflammatory process. The absence of joint line tenderness and the presence of fluctuance indicate that the issue is likely related to a fluid-filled structure rather than the joint itself. The most likely underlying cause of these symptoms is inflammation of a periarticular fluid-filled sac, such as a prepatellar bursa, which can become inflamed due to repetitive trauma or overuse, common in mechanics. Other options like infection or crystal deposition are less likely given the presentation and lack of systemic symptoms. Therefore, the best-supported option is inflammation of the periarticular fluid-filled sac.
